Fixtures copied from https://github.com/markokr/rarfile/tree/master/test/files
rar5-crc.rar, rar3-solid.rar, rar5-psw.rar and rar5-hpsw.rar.
Encrypted fixtures use the test password "password". Copyright and permission: LICENSE.
rar5-solid.rar added from the same repository at d2f7df6fc843dae356fd6b0a85971dc36fd6e757.

RAR3/RAR5 multi-volume session fixtures added from the same pinned repository:
https://github.com/markokr/rarfile/tree/d2f7df6fc843dae356fd6b0a85971dc36fd6e757/test/files
Permission is the accompanying LICENSE (ISC permission notice).
These are real stored, NON-SOLID archives; they do not establish solid
dictionary continuity across volumes. Upstream metadata is recorded in
rar3-vols.part1.rar.exp and rar5-vols.part1.rar.exp at that commit.

Known expected bytes (verified independently from the stored RAR3 blocks):
vols/bigfile.txt: concatenate fmt.Sprintf("%40d\n", i), i=1..5000.
  205000 bytes, CRC32 509ad74c (also in upstream .exp), SHA256
  57613b4a0d18b31472c9abe90780dcaf834f4edf48e79008f027a99710cf3632
vols/smallfile.txt: concatenate fmt.Sprintf("%40d\n", i), i=1..50.
  2050 bytes, CRC32 d08a1f86 (also in upstream .exp), SHA256
  6805973b24128edda3148235c77a7f7b5a7a9be6272bc882a6e030871b2b18d1
Both RAR versions contain these same two members. Tests construct these bytes
directly, without using a second rardecode decoder as the content oracle.

Corrupt variants are generated only in memory by the tests. Solid fixtures
have the second member's declared data CRC changed and header CRC recomputed;
the original compressed stream and solid continuation remain intact. Split
stored fixtures have one payload byte changed in part2 (offset 200), with all
headers unchanged. Missing-volume tests expose only part1 to the session.

Generated compressed solid multipart fixtures (not copied upstream):
rar3-solid-multipart.part01.rar through part04.rar
rar5-solid-multipart.part01.rar through part04.rar
Generator and generated data/archives: LICENSE.generated (BSD-2-Clause).
No RAR/UNRAR binary or other tool component is distributed with the fixtures.

Creator: official RAR 6.24 Linux x64, 3 October 2023, used temporarily.
Primary source: https://www.rarlab.com/rar/rarlinux-x64-624.tar.gz
Tool package SHA256:
88e22a8e84125c947637bbf28c746e338a0a63279d80f9f9d7373603875db1eb
RAR executable SHA256 (enforced by the generator):
71ab9088d575e438d243672fcc6d36d2f9a39f5a8d4d26e998129cea12dbf682
The package license permits evaluation use for up to 40 days (section 2)
and states no additional fees for archive/volume creation and distribution
(section 7). The proprietary tool's license is separate from generated data.
The official release notes explain that RAR 7 removed RAR4 creation:
https://www.rarlab.com/rarnew.htm

Reproduce into an empty directory, supplying an external official RAR binary:
python3 tests/fixtures/rar/generate_solid_multipart.py --rar <RAR-6.24> --out <OUTPUT>
The generator sets TZ=UTC, LC_ALL=C, mode 0644 and mtime 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z.
Archive command (FORMAT=4 for the legacy v29 decoder fixture, FORMAT=5 for RAR5):
rar a -cfg- -maFORMAT -m3 -md256k -s -sv- -v16384b -mt1 -ep -ts- -oi0 -idq rarVERSION-solid-multipart.rar first.bin second.bin
The tool's manual describes -sv- as disabling solid-statistics reset across
volumes. -oi0 avoids identical-file references. Legacy archives have the RAR
1.5/3/4 container signature and v29 compressed data; these are not RAR5.

Input is wholly synthetic: xorshift32 seed 0x86, shifts 13/17/5 with uint32
arithmetic; take the low byte of each updated state 49152 times and concatenate
that block twice. Both first.bin and second.bin contain exactly those bytes.
Each member is 98304 bytes, CRC32 8469b249, SHA256:
04bdbf62c09c8fe4899c780f22302811a45d787bbfea06df80f7ab642876099e
Go tests independently implement this byte generator as their content oracle.
Both versions expand to 196608 bytes each; all eight volumes total 99734 bytes.
Two generator runs produced identical archive hashes. Independent official
UNRAR 7.12 (1993-2025 Alexander Roshal) verified both archives with `unrar t`
and each member's exact bytes with `unrar p -inul -p- ARCHIVE MEMBER`.
Verifier executable SHA256:
32a2b4cbdd260f9ecb8a84e5ceae521e078311e6ec610d8804ea5355adf68483

first.bin has a genuinely compressed stream split across all four volumes.
second.bin starts in volume four, has Solid=true and is only 69 packed bytes
(legacy v29) or 23 packed bytes (RAR5), depending on preceding dictionary data.
Skipping the first member's packed blocks without decoding, then constructing
a fresh decoder for second.bin, yields ErrBadFileChecksum and different bytes
in both versions. Tests do not simulate solid behavior by changing stored flags.
These initial generated samples are unencrypted; the encrypted variants below
demonstrate the encrypted-solid-multipart combination separately.

Encrypted solid multipart variants:
rar3-solid-encrypted-multipart.part01.rar through part04.rar
rar5-solid-encrypted-multipart.part01.rar through part04.rar
Same synthetic inputs, official tool and LICENSE.generated as the clear set.
The public password "password" belongs ONLY to these synthetic test fixtures;
it is not an account credential or a password for user data.
Generate with the preceding script plus --encrypted; archive commands add
the literal fixture switch -ppassword. Headers remain readable, while file
contents are encrypted. The first member crosses four volumes, and the second
member in volume four is marked Solid and Encrypted in both versions.

The plaintext is reproducible and has the same fixed member hash recorded
above. Encryption uses random salt/IV: two generator runs produced different
archive hashes in all eight volumes, so encrypted archives are NOT promised
to be bit-identical. The current committed volumes are frozen by hashes below.
These eight archives total 100221 bytes; expansion is 393216 bytes combined.
Independent official UNRAR 7.12 `t -ppassword` verified both archives and
`p -inul -ppassword ARCHIVE MEMBER` matched each member's exact generated bytes.
UNRAR rejected the wrong synthetic password with exit 3 (legacy) / 11 (RAR5).
In rardecode the wrong-password terminal error is ErrBadFileChecksum (legacy)
or ErrBadPassword (RAR5); all successfully opened files are released once.
